title: 1. Articles (Articles: A, An, The, -)
rulesEn: A: Used before singular countable nouns starting with a consonant sound (e.g., a university, a train).
An: Used before singular countable nouns starting with a vowel sound (e.g., an hour, an M.A., an apple).
The: Used for specific items, unique things, or previously mentioned nouns (e.g., the sun, the train).
- (Zero Article): Used for general plural nouns, proper names, or abstract concepts.
explanationNp: व्यञ्जन ध्वनि (Consonant Sound) अगाडि 'a', स्वर ध्वनि (Vowel Sound) अगाडि 'an', र कुनै खास वा निश्चित वस्तु/नदी/प्रसिद्ध चीजको अगाडि 'the' को प्रयोग गरिन्छ।
examples: an hour (starts with /o/ vowel sound) h is silent
the train had stopped (referring to the specific train mentioned earlier)

title: 2. Matching & Preposition Phrases
rulesEn: Time Bounds: 'may have left by now' indicates expected completion by the current moment.
Duration: 'all through the night' covers the entire duration of the night.
Exception: 'apart from the wet weather' excludes weather from the condition.
Location: 'under my jacket', 'inside the house', 'on the table'.
explanationNp: वाक्य जोड्दा वा Preposition छान्दा अर्थ र समय (Time) को ध्यान दिनुपर्छ। जस्तै: by now (अहिलेसम्ममा), all through the night (रातभरि)।
examples: The last bus may have left + by now.
I think they're on + the table.

title: 3. Sentence Structure & Word Order
rulesEn: Standard Formula: Subject + Verb + Object + Infinitive/Prepositional Phrase.
Step 1: Identify who is performing the action (Subject).
Step 2: Find the main verb or expectation verb (e.g., expected, planning).
Step 3: Attach infinitive phrase (e.g., to arrive on time, to hire).
explanationNp: सबैभन्दा पहिले मुख्य Subject (कर्ता) र Verb (क्रिया) पहिचान गर्नुहोस्। त्यसपछि Object (कर्म) र अन्त्यमा तोकिएको टुक्रा (Infinitive: to + V1) जोड्नुहोस्।
examples: Infinitive phrase: to arrive on time
Full: The principal expected the teachers to arrive on time.
